A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BirdSet study and contain readable main text and Appendices A–E. Text, equations, tables, and figures can be reliably matched despite layout changes.

before.justification: v4 reports original model evaluations across three training scenarios in Section 4 and Tables 9–11, plus validation and species-level inference analyses in Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v5 retains these original benchmark results and appendix analyses. Results retained from v4 remain original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: The training procedures, architectures, binary cross-entropy loss, augmentations, and inference-time logit restrictions remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions use XCL/XCM, dedicated training subsets, VOX augmentation data, POW validation, and the same seven soundscape test datasets. Epic Sounds disappears from survey Table 7 but was not used experimentally.

E2.justification: The benchmark retains EfficientNet, ConvNext, AST, EAT, W2V2, and Perch in their corresponding comparisons. Appendix D still compares ConvNext with Perch, and BirdNET remains excluded because of potential test leakage.

E3.justification: Training budgets, preprocessing, five-second evaluation segments, validation choices, and cmAP/AUROC/T1-Acc metrics are unchanged. Expanded captions restate existing training settings rather than introduce new protocols.

E4.justification: Dataset-distribution analyses in Figures 7–9, validation-loss analysis in Figure 10, and HSN/POW inference analyses in Figures 14–15 are retained unchanged. No ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Seed-count statements and mean/standard-deviation reporting in Section 4.1, Table 8, and Tables 9–11 remain unchanged. No statistical test or uncertainty-estimation procedure is added.

E6.justification: Table 7 removes the descriptive quantitative comparison for Epic Sounds, listed in v4 as 100 hours and 44 classes. Model scores in Tables 3 and 9–11, plotted results, and reported experimental findings are unchanged; this is a limited loss of dataset-comparison information, not a performance change.

T1.justification: The metric definitions and equations in Appendix C.5 are unchanged. Explaining J in Table 2's caption repeats the existing evenness-index explanation in Section 3 rather than introducing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows its criticism of AudioSet from suitability as the primary resource to adequacy as the sole resource; the introduction explicitly calls BirdSet an additional resource. Claims about BirdSet's scale, coverage, accessibility, and benchmark contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 now attributes incomplete real-world coverage to limited dataset size and quantity. Section 2.2 qualifies the claimed restriction on real-world applicability as a potential difficulty handling overlapping sounds and event ambiguity. Interpretations of the benchmark results and the paper's own limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware descriptions, preprocessing instructions, and reported code, data, checkpoint, and experiment-log access remain unchanged. Removing 'internal' from the backup-server description in Appendix B.2 does not change access or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: BirdSet is positioned more explicitly as complementary to AudioSet. Tables 6–7 replace iNaturalist/iNatSounds website citations with Chasmai et al. (2024), updating attribution for already discussed resources; the Epic Sounds row and Huh et al. reference are removed.

P1.justification: There are localized wording revisions in the abstract, contribution list, and Sections 2.1–2.2, plus citation-formatting and punctuation fixes. The main narrative and appendix section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 explains J, and Table 3 and Figure 6 expand their training-context captions. Table 7 loses one row and shares a page with Figures 7–8; Figures 12–13 move alongside their corresponding result tables. The plotted content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: Clearer captions, more qualified comparisons with prior datasets, and pairing appendix plots with their tables modestly improve readability and precision while preserving the benchmark evidence. Removing Epic Sounds from Table 7 and the references while retaining it in Figure 1 slightly reduces traceability, but does not outweigh these limited presentation gains.
